newsitem.title: USA: Bob Dole says wife might run for president.
newsitem.headline: Bob Dole says wife might run for president.

text.p: Bob Dole said Monday that his wife Elizabeth might run for president in 2000.
"She might," Dole told NBC's "Today Show" when asked if Elizabeth Dole will run for president. "I'd like to see her to do what she thinks she can to make a difference."
Elizabeth Dole, 60, head of the Red Cross and a former cabinet member, has said she would not rule out running for office.

She recently said she has no plans to run for president and wants to devote full time to the Red Cross. "Politics -- that's not something that's on the agenda for me now," she said Jan. 2 when she resumed working at the Red Cross after taking a leave of absence to help her husband run for president.
Bob Dole said he has not made up his mind about what he plans to do, possibly joining a law firm or writing a book, but did not rule out a return to public life.
Dole had high praise for Clinton, saying he had a good personal relationship with him. "I respect him as a person, as a president, yes, and we have a good relationship, as far as I know," Dole said.

"If the president of the United States asked me to do something, say some foreign policy, to help in some way, I would certainly look at it very seriously if he did it in a non-partisan, non-political, genuine effort to reach out, not to Bob Dole, but to somewhere, maybe I could be helpful."
Asked whether House Speaker Newt Gingrich's ethical problems bothered him, Dole said "I think Newt's going to have some rehab -- He's going to have to work at it."

"He's going to have to demonstrate to the American people ... the bottom line is they want to trust their leaders. They want someone they can believe in, they can trust and I think Newt is going to work very hard regaining that trust."
"I think he needs to, for the House, the party and the country," Dole said.
